correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the first-table fiber proves the full PGF as a binomial mixture of independent Bernoulli contributions. An exhaustive zero-event partition yields the exact reliability formula. Balanced sparse sampling has per-key one-violation probability ab/q+o(1/q) and negligible multi-violations; asymmetric sampling has a rare single Y fact per key with Bin(q-1,p_q) mismatches tending to Poisson(a). Independent keys and generating-function limits prove the claimed weak laws, and direct summation gives EW=q²(q−1)pr and the shared limit ab. Finite exhaustive q<=3 full-histogram and 56 numerical identity checks were successfully replayed; these are supporting evidence, not the proof.

value.rationale: The atom is a natural cross-table integrity and consistency property; its exact Bernoulli satisfaction probability and full violation distribution quantify error severity. The strict difference e^{-b(1-e^{-a})}>e^{-ab} at equal limiting mean ab identifies a natural balanced-versus-imbalanced sparsity boundary and a genuine clustering mechanism that cannot be read off from expectation or textbook Poisson approximation alone. The contribution is a motivated structural limiting-law contrast, not a recomputation of isolated small counts.
